purpose: The 404 page's only content section: a two-tone h1, one outline CTA and a looping theme-paired artwork.

headingAccent.note: Measured: 2 words, "is broken", in a .u-fonts-50 span inside the same h1.

alt.note: Required on every content image. Measured 3-27 words across the real images (longest: a 27-word hero carousel description); the four decorative preloader images ship alt="", which is why the empty string is allowed. alt is accessibility text, not visible page copy, so it carries its own budget but is excluded from contentMaxWordsTotal.

artwork.note: A theme pair: the .theme-dark member ships visible and the .theme-light member hidden, even though the page renders LIGHT.

evidence.structure: Structure and copy measured from the live original's own 404 page.

constraints.verification: src/pages/NotFound.jsx:8 renders <NotFoundContent /> as the only child of <Layout>. Checked against all 5 real templates: it appears only in `not-found`, where - because that template has no chrome.menu - it is the node immediately after chrome.header.

artwork.note: The only two .webp files in the whole project.

motion.detail: The h1 carries data-hero-text, so public/motion/m25.js reveals it with the 0.2 stagger and the data-final-opacity rule. The artwork loops inside .hero__404__loop. public/motion/m11.js owns the theme pair swap.
motion.reducedMotionFallback: Show the h1 and the CTA at final opacity with no stagger, and hold the artwork on its first frame.
motion.reducedMotionFallbackKind: design-rule (the source ships NO prefers-reduced-motion handling for this section, so the fallback is prescribed by this repository, not mirrored)

responsive.base: heading.page 5.5rem; the loop layers are 103rem wide

notes: The section reuses id="hero" (the same DOM id the home hero uses) but a different class, hero__404__wrap. The two never co-occur, because no template contains both hero.home and hero.not-found, so the duplicate id is not a conflict in practice.
contentMaxWordsTotalNote: Set BETWEEN the measured real total and the maximum the per-field budgets allow, so the cap can actually reject an over-long instance instead of being unreachable. extraction/verify_all.py check [p] fails if any declared contentMaxWordsTotal becomes vacuous (>= the per-field maximum). Previously 35, which was unreachable.
